title: Annotatio IV §.XXI open: Waldenses old and new — Supper sentence passes to the Reformed in Age XVII
pass_a_gloss: §. XXI. The sentence of the Waldenses, both Old and New, concerning the Sacred Supper — although sometimes proposed more obscurely (which we will easily grant to the Lutheran Theologians cited above) — yet in the XVIIth AGE passed over to that most potent part of the Protestants, i.e. of those opposing Papism, which to this day comes under the name of the REFORMED.
pass_b_english: §.XXI: the Waldenses’ Supper sentence — old and new — is sometimes obscure (as the Lutheran critics said), yet in Age XVII it passed to the chief anti-papal Protestant wing.
That wing still bears the name REFORMED.
source_text: §. XXI. Waldensium tàm Veterum, quàm Novorum, de Sacra Cœna sententia, etsi quandoque (quod citatis retrò Theologis Lutheranis facile dabimus) obscurius proposita, SECULO XVII ad istam tamen potissimum Protestantium, i.e. Papismum oppugnantium, partem transiit, quæ REFORMATORUM nomine hodieque venit.
